article.title: Iranian Security Forces Continue Crackdown on Protestors; 38 detained in Qazvin
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Persian article.
Iran's intelligence forces are continuing their crackdown on people who took part in the late December 2025 to January 2026 anti-regime protests.

In its most recent report, the Intelligence Directorate of Qazvin Province claimed to have arrested 39 people in connection with the demonstrations. In a statement, Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence described the detainees as “mercenaries of the American-Zionist enemy” and alleged that they had been operating in eight organized groups.

The ministry alleged that the detainees were involved in damaging and setting fire to homes, banks, public and personal vehicles, and a gas station on Shahid Babaei Street in Qazvin City, as well as looting stores and government premises. The statement further accused 10 of the detainees of killing an unspecified number of security personnel.

The statement's claims could not be independently verified. International rights groups strongly dispute the Iranian regime's narrative. Independent human rights organizations, including Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, and UN-mandated bodies, have consistently characterized similar charges against protesters as fabricated and politically motivated.

Rights groups highlight that the Islamic Republic routinely relies on forced, televised confessions extracted under torture and solitary confinement to justify harsh sentencing and bypass due process. Detainees are routinely denied access to legal counsel or fair trials.

The protests began in Tehran on December 28, 2025, and rapidly spread nationwide, fueled by public anger over regime mismanagement, systemic corruption, and a severe economic crisis. Slogans chanted by demonstrators called for the downfall of the Islamic Republic. While official state reports attempt to minimize the scale of the state violence, international observers report that tens of thousands of Iranians were killed or arbitrarily detained as security forces used lethal force to suppress the demonstrations.

The announcement of new arrests in Qazvin follows a series of similar state media releases. A few days earlier, the Ministry of Intelligence reported detaining 11 individuals in Malekshahi County, Ilam Province, alongside earlier announcements of 31 arrests in Sirjan and 126 in Tehran Province.

Judicial cases have since been opened against many of those swept up in the nationwide raids. The charges brought by state prosecutors include assembly and collusion against national security, destruction of property, and "corruption on Earth" - a capital offense under the Islamic Republic's legal code that carries the death penalty and has frequently been condemned by human rights defenders as a tool used to silence dissent.
zh: 伊朗安全部隊持續鎮壓抗議者；卡茲溫有38人遭拘留
編者註：本報導翻譯自美國之音波斯語版原文。
伊朗情報部門正持續鎮壓那些曾參與2025年12月底至2026年1月反政府抗議活動的人士。
卡茲溫省情報局在其最新報告中聲稱，已逮捕39名與示威活動有關的人士。伊朗情報部在一份聲明中將這些被捕者描述為「美以敵人的傭兵」，並指控他們以八個有組織的團體形式進行活動。
該部指控，這些被拘留者涉嫌在卡茲溫市沙希德·巴巴伊街破壞並縱火焚燒民宅、銀行、公共及私人車輛，以及一座加油站，並洗劫商店和政府建築。該聲明進一步指控其中10名被拘留者殺害了數量不詳的安全人員。
該聲明所載的指控無法經由獨立渠道核實。國際人權團體強烈反駁伊朗政權的說法。包括國際特赦組織、人權觀察以及聯合國授權機構在內的獨立人權組織，一貫將針對抗議者的類似指控定性為捏造且出於政治動機。
人權團體指出，伊朗伊斯蘭共和國經常利用在酷刑和單獨監禁下逼供而得、並經電視直播的供詞，作為頒布嚴厲判決及繞過正當法律程序的依據。被拘留者經常被剝奪尋求法律諮詢或獲得公平審判的權利。
抗議活動於2025年12月28日在德黑蘭爆發，並迅速蔓延至全國各地，其導火線是民眾對政權管理不善、制度性貪腐以及嚴峻經濟危機的憤怒。 示威者高呼的口號要求推翻伊斯蘭共和國。儘管官方報告試圖淡化國家暴力行為的規模，但國際觀察員指出，安全部隊動用致命武力鎮壓示威活動，導致數萬名伊朗人遭殺害或任意拘留。
卡茲溫傳出新一批逮捕消息之前，官方媒體已發布過一系列類似的公告。數天前，情報部通報在伊拉姆省馬萊克沙希縣拘留了11人；此前，官方還曾宣布在西爾詹逮捕了31人，以及在德黑蘭省逮捕了126人。
此後，針對在全國性突襲行動中遭逮捕的許多人，已分別提起司法訴訟。 州檢察官提出的指控包括：危害國家安全的集會與串謀、毀壞財產，以及「在世上作惡」——根據伊斯蘭共和國的法律，這是一項可判處死刑的死罪，並經常被人權捍衛者譴責為用來壓制異見的工具。
